title: Trajectory of Sequential Machine Composition
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and symbol alphabet, with state sets $S_1$ and $S_2$. Fix an entry state $e_1$ and an exit state $f_1$ of $M_1$, an entry state $e_2$ of $M_2$, and a contract $C_1$ for $M_1$ whose entry is $e_1$ and whose exit set is exactly $some(f_1)$. For a parameter $i$ and a configuration $d$ of the machine with state set $S_1\oplus S_2$, suppose $d$ is in state $(e_1,\mathrm{inl})$ and replacing its state by $e_1$ gives a configuration satisfying $C_1$'s precondition for $i$. At every time $u$ up to and including the contract running time, the composed machine's run from $d$ equals the $M_1$ run from that state-replaced configuration with states mapped into the left summand, and the latter run has a nonempty state. For every $v$, the composed run at the contract running time plus one plus $v$ equals the $M_2$ run from the contract endpoint with its state replaced by $e_2$, mapped into the right summand; that state-replaced endpoint is in state $e_2$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1$ and $M_2$ have the same number of work tapes and symbol alphabet
$e_1$ and $f_1$ are states of $M_1$; $e_2$ is a state of $M_2$
$C_1$ is a contract for $M_1$ with entry $e_1$ and exit set exactly $some(f_1)$
$d$ is a configuration of the composed machine and is in state $(e_1,\mathrm{inl})$
Replacing the state of $d$ by $e_1$ satisfies $C_1$'s precondition for $i$
replaced:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines with the same number of work tapes and
symbol alphabet, with state sets $S_1$ and $S_2$. Suppose a contract for $M_1$, entered
at $e_1\in S_1$ and exiting at $e_1'\in S_1$, has precondition, running time, endpoint,
and head envelope as specified by the contract. For any parameter $i$ and configuration
$d$ whose state is $(e_1,\mathrm{inl})$, assume the configuration obtained by replacing
every state of $d$ by $e_1$ satisfies the contract precondition. Up to and including the
contract running time, the composed machine follows the $M_1$ trajectory with states
embedded in $S_1\oplus S_2$, and that trajectory never halts; after one additional step,
its trajectory is the $M_2$ trajectory from the contract endpoint with every nonhalting
state replaced by the entry state $e_2\in S_2$, embedded in $S_1\oplus S_2$. In
particular, that modified endpoint has state $e_2$.
